title: Electromotive force
content: Electromotive force, abbreviated as emf is the amount of energy, provided by the battery, per unit charge to move round the complete circuit.
e: Electromotive force, abbreviated as emf is the amount of energy, provided by the battery, per unit charge to move round the complete circuit. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

title: Terminal voltage (Available Voltage)
content: The potential difference across the terminals of a battery connected to an external circuit is called the terminal voltage (or available voltage) of the battery.
e: Terminal voltage (Available Voltage): The potential difference across the terminals of a battery connected to an external circuit is called the terminal voltage (or available voltage) of the battery. Terminal voltage is emf minus Ir, so it sags when the load current rises.

title: Electrical energy
content: Electrical energy is energy associated with the flow of charge through any part of circuit.
e: Electrical energy is energy associated with the flow of charge through any part of circuit. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

title: Electrical power
content: Electrical power is the rate of transfer of electrical energy.
e: Electrical power is the rate of transfer of electrical energy. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

title: Joule's law
content: Joule's law stated as the amount of heat produced in a resistor due to a current flowing through it is directly proportional to the square of the current, the value of resistance and the time taken by the current to pass through the resistor.
e: Joule's law stated as the amount of heat produced in a resistor due to a current flowing through it is directly proportional to the square of the current, the value of resistance and the time taken by the current to pass through the resistor. Joule heat is I^2 R t; it grows with current squared.

title: Fuse
content: A fuse is a thin short wire of tin - lead alloy which is used in electric circuits to prevent electrical appliances from being damaged if excessive current flows through them.
e: Fuse: A fuse is a thin short wire of tin - lead alloy which is used in electric circuits to prevent electrical appliances from being damaged if excessive current flows through them. A fuse is a thin tin-lead wire that melts on overload and opens the circuit on purpose.

title: Light bulb
content: An electrical light bulb is made of a glass bulb consisting a tungsten filament which has high melting point ( ~3000 °C)
e: Light bulb: An electrical light bulb is made of a glass bulb consisting a tungsten filament which has high melting point ( ~3000 °C). The bulb filament is tungsten because it can sit near 3000 °C without melting.
